ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly high-intensity (white) across approximately 90% of the visible surface, with high-contrast low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels restricted to the trailing edge boundary and the distal tips.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white field across both fluke lobes; low-intensity dark pigmentation forms a continuous linear band along the entire trailing edge and encapsulates the distal tips; sparse dark focal spots (~5-10 pixels in diameter) are located near the central median area.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped central depression with an estimated interior angle of 55-65 degrees and a vertical depth approximately 1/8th of the fluke's visible height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, low-amplitude micro-serrations (saw-tooth pattern) distributed uniformly along the trailing edge; individual pixel peaks are clearly defined against the lighter water background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly convex curvature on the posterior edge of both lobes, tapering to narrow, slightly rounded distal points.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Small dark circular clusters visible in the lower-central region near the junction with the peduncle; several isolated white pin-point clusters on the dark trailing edge border.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Three distinct, brownish-tinted diagonal linear disruptions on the right lobe (viewer perspective) extending from the mid-surface toward the trailing edge.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: The distal end of the right lobe (viewer perspective) exhibits a jagged, irregular amputation or traumatic notch distinct from the natural serration pattern.
other_distinctive_markers: Prominent vertical golden-orange specular reflection (sun glare) localized on the left side of the peduncle and lower central fluke.
